questions.text: Which one of the following fields of an IP header is NOT modified by a typical IP router?
questions.solution:
Routers decrease TTL, recompute the checksum, and change the length when they fragment. The source address stays the same (unless NAT is used, which is not typical routing).

Answer: Source address

questions.text: In one of the pairs of protocols given below, both the protocols can use multiple TCP connections between the same client and the server. Which one is that?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- HTTP: a browser can open several parallel TCP connections to the same server.
- FTP: uses a control connection plus separate data connections.

TELNET and SMTP use a single connection.

Answer: HTTP, FTP

questions.text:
For any two languages L1 and L2 such that L1 is context-free and L2 is recursively enumerable but not recursive, which of the following is/are necessarily true?
I. [latex]\bar{L_{1}}[/latex] (complement of L1) is recursive
II. [latex] \bar{L_{2}}[/latex] (complement of L2) is recursive
III. [latex]\bar{L_{1}}[/latex] is context-free
IV. [latex]\bar{L_{1}} \cup L_{2}[/latex] is recursively enumerable
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: CFLs are decidable, and recursive languages are closed under complement [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- II: if [latex]\bar L_2[/latex] were recursive, L2 would be recursive [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False
- III: CFLs are not closed under complement [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not necessarily
- IV: [latex]\bar L_1[/latex] is recursive (so RE), and RE is closed under union [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True

Answer: I and IV only

questions.text: Consider a system with byte-addressable memory, 32-bit logical addresses, 4 kilobyte page size and page table entries of 4 bytes each. The size of the page table in the system in megabytes is ________ .
questions.solution:
Number of pages = [latex]\frac{2^{32}}{2^{12}}=2^{20}[/latex]

Page table size = [latex]2^{20}\times4[/latex] B = 4 MB

Answer: 4

questions.text:
The following two functions P1 and P2 that share a variable B with an initial value of 2 execute concurrently.

The number of distinct values that B can possibly take after the execution is______________.
questions.solution:
B = 2 initially. Possible results:

- P1 then P2: C = 1, B = 2; D = 4, B = 3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3
- P2 then P1: D = 4, B = 3; C = 2, B = 4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4
- Both read B = 2 first (C = 1, D = 4), and P1 writes last: B = 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2

Distinct values {2, 3, 4} = 3

Answer: 3
